correctness.rationale: Explicit commuting reciprocal and hyperelliptic involutions yield two genus-two quotients v^2=(t±2)(t^4-4t^2+2+a). Kani–Rosen eigenspaces give Jac(C)~Jac(D+)×Jac(D-). The minus quotient is a (-1)-twist of the plus quotient; when p=13 it is isomorphic and when p=11 its odd Frobenius coefficients vanish. For genus-two functional equations, exhaustive N1=p+1 and N2=p²+1+2b determine numerator 1+bT²+p²T⁴. Independent quadratic-field character-sum computation covered both quotient signs, every a with a²!=4, and both Fp and Fp² for p=11,13, exactly matching published tables (9 distinct b for each p; two collision pairs in p=13). Geometric nonisomorphism for a²!=a’² uses Ohashi–Kudo Prop3.2.4; Tate’s finite-field criterion gives isogenous unpolarized Jacobians. Finite tables are exhaustive in two indicated primes; all extension degrees follow from the genus-two zeta polynomial, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: The exact finite classification of all smooth parameters in each specified natural small characteristic yields concrete equal-zeta/nonisomorphic pairs, a useful test case separating curve geometry from Jacobian isogeny. The novel object is the complete arithmetic table and its consequences, not the already known reciprocal involutions.

final_claim: For p=11,13 all smooth genus-four curves y^2=x^9+a x^5+x with a^2!=4 have P=(1+bT^2+p^2T^4)^2, with exhaustive b(a) tables; for p=13 precisely a={3,5} and {8,10} collide in Weil spectrum while being geometrically nonisomorphic and having base-field isogenous Jacobians.
limitations: Smooth normalized family a²!=4 only, p=11 or p=13; isogenous unpolarized Jacobians, not principally polarized isomorphism; no all-genus-four census.
